about: MUTATING — delete the forge registry's image versions that no train, no rollback and no cluster can want any more (infra/forge/prune-registry-versions.sh <mode> [keep_trains [max_delete]]). Backlog 9789a827, David 2026-09-17 (the replacement disk was not delivered; 'that order sounds great' — buy the headroom). Measured 2026-09-16: /opt/forgejo/data is 93 GB of the forge's 228 GB disk — the container registry every train pushes a boss:<sha> image to (1–3 GB each, plus boss-ci:<sha> per train) — and nothing pruned the REGISTRY side: prune-registry-tags.lib.sh removes LOCAL docker tags only after the registry holds them (the registry is the rollback path), disk-floor-sweep stops at its floor, and the registry grows ~2 GB per train. Measured 2026-09-17: 1,423 container versions; docker push stores a tag (its one file is the OCI index) plus two untagged sha256 children where the layers live, so the script reads EVERY tag's index through /v2 before classifying and deletes a child only when every tag referencing it goes. THE KEEP SET IS DERIVED, and a half that cannot be derived is a refusal that deletes nothing: the live images (every owner image the cluster runs; deploy/boss in namespace boss required — the watchdog's own read), the rollback target (the converge's last-built stamp the watchdog rolls to by name), the last N landed trains' shas (landed-train-shas.lib.sh over the newest 2N pr-train packets; keep_trains, default 10), latest, everything newer than 24 h, and everything unclassifiable (a tag that is not a sha, an unreadable index, every orphan while any index was unreadable). THE CREDENTIAL is the converge's own docker login for the registry host (the checkout owner's ~/.docker/config.json), used as Basic on the packages API and as a bearer minted at /v2/token for the manifest reads; it rides in a curl config file, never argv, and is never printed. A 403 refuses NAMING THE SCOPE the forge asks for — read:package on the listing, write:package on the first DELETE — a ceremony for David, and the real run stops on that first DELETE. --dry-run derives the keep set, reads the registry and prints the plan (would DELETE / unclassified, by name) and the record; --for-real DELETEs tags first, then children, judged by HTTP code (204 gone, 404 already gone, anything else stops with the count so far on the record), and prints each planned version with its OUTCOME as the verb — DELETED / GONE / FAILED <code> / KEPT — never would DELETE (backlog ea67ad87: the first real run, ops-request 973beaa2, 2026-09-17, printed the plan file as-is and appended the outcomes after the runner's 100 KB cut, so the packet read 898 conditionals under an OK verdict). The record is ONE JSON line: kept/delete/deleted/unclassified per package, the keep halves, listed versus the forge's total, and df of the data directory before and after — bytes are not claimed because the packages API declares no sizes and Forgejo's [cron.cleanup_packages] frees the blobs later (measured on that first real run: 1,337 deleted, df moved 724 KB); its cadence is not in this tree, so the record's cleanup_cron carries SCHEDULE and OLDER_THAN read off the forge's own app.ini under the data directory, or says the file could not be read; read df on the packet after that cron has run. The record and the verdict line come BEFORE the per-version list (backlog 5323f3ef, 2026-09-17: 1,313 lines and the record last, cut off by the runner's 100 KB window), and the full list is /var/backups/boss/registry-prune/<stamp>.txt on the forge, named in the record as list_file. THE CEILING A HAND RUN MAY NAME (backlog 1bef55a6): a plan past 1,500 versions or 90% of the two packages' versions is refused before the first DELETE, and the fraction grows with the backlog — the keep set is roughly constant, so after about eight days without a run the plan passes 90% (ee6caa74 planned 89.6%), exactly when the registry most needs the prune — and a packet could not lift it (the bounds were env only). The lifts are bounded, not approved (the adversarial review of 1bef55a6, finding 3: the approval contract's signed plan_sha256 would void before the runner ran, because a registry prune's plan moves with every push and every hour of the 24 h window). An optional third arg, max_delete (1..3000, twice the default), replaces the ABSOLUTE bound for that one run, rides the packet's args and the record's ceiling.source = argv, and still binds; to name it, name keep_trains too (10 is the default): --for-real 10 1800. The 90% fraction always holds; it is lifted only by a larger keep_trains, which keeps more landed trains and so plans less, never deleting what the default keep set keeps — a backlog is walked down run by run. Each ceiling refusal names the lift that fits it, with a 20% margin on a suggested max_delete. The daily verb takes no argument, so an unattended run keeps both bounds. A PASS THAT JUDGED TOO LITTLE FAILS (exit 1): with no bearer from /v2/token, every manifest read failing, or under 90% of the tags' indexes read, tags and orphans are held and the plan shrinks toward 0, and 'deleted 0 of 0' is not a verdict; the record and the unclassified list are still printed. A DELETE's answer is not its effect (review finding 1): a real run lists the registry again after its deletes, and fails when a planned version is still listed (STILL LISTED, by name), when the re-list cannot be read, or when every DELETE answered 404 (what a moved route answers to everything). The OK verdict's count is the planned versions the re-list no longer holds, with how many answered 404, the indexes read and their percentage, and the unclassified count; the record keeps deleted (204) and gone (404) apart and carries relist.still_listed. A LISTING MUST BE WHOLE (the re-review of 1bef55a6): the first listing is refused, deleting nothing, when it read fewer versions than the forge's X-Total-Count, when that count is not a number (it is checked before anything prints it), or when a live, rollback or latest tag is missing from it; the re-list must also be whole and must list again every version the run kept, or the run fails. The verdict line carries listed L of T, and the daily watch judges listed >= total. Own timeout: one listing page per 50 versions, one manifest read per tag, one DELETE per version. The switch-instance-database shape and process: an explicit per-verb authorization, a precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default.
